question.text: Under the Fourth Schedule of SEBI (AIF) Regulations (Code of Conduct for AIFs), which of the following is an obligation of an AIF?

answer.text: Operate in the interest of ALL investors and not merely the Sponsor/Manager/directors or a select class; maintain written conflict-of-interest policies; maintain AML policies; ensure timely and accurate dissemination of information; not use unethical means to sell
Operate primarily in the interest of the Manager to maximise carried interest
Provide information only to investors who contribute more than 10% of corpus
Conflicts of interest need not be disclosed if they affect less than 5% of fund assets

explanation.text: The Logic: Fourth Schedule of SEBI (AIF) Regulations lists Code of Conduct items: (a) invest per PPM objectives, (b) operate in interest of ALL investors, (c) disseminate adequate/accurate/explicit/timely information, (d) effective risk management, (e) written conflict-of-interest policies, (f) no unethical sales, (g) written AML policies. Key-personnel code also exists. The Trap: Options B/C/D either invert, narrow, or dilute the code. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B test Code of Conduct at selling level. XIX-C tests Manager-side obligations including pari-passu and pro-rata rights. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: Refresh the conflict-of-interest policy annually; cover related-party transactions (75% investor approval threshold), priority distribution model (banned post-18 Nov 2024), and side-letter differential rights (disclose in PPM). Compliance Officer signs the Compliance Test Report under Reg 20A framework.
